name: Ibn Zaydun
bio: Abu al-Walid Ahmad ibn Abdallah ibn Ahmad ibn Ghalib ibn Zaydun al-Makhzumi was a vizier, prose writer and poet of Cordoba, born in 394 AH (1004 CE); Ibn Khallikan says he came of one of the city's leading families of jurists. He attached himself to Ibn Jahwar, one of the party kings, and served as his envoy to the other rulers of al-Andalus, until Ibn Jahwar suspected him of leaning towards al-Mu'tadid ibn Abbad and imprisoned him; his letters pleading for mercy failed, and he escaped. He went over to al-Mu'tadid, ruler of Seville, who made him his vizier (Ibn Khallikan dates the move to 441 AH, 1049 CE), and he stayed in favour until he died in Seville in Rajab 463 AH (1071 CE), under al-Mu'tadid's son al-Mu'tamid. He loved Wallada, daughter of al-Mustakfi, whose salon in Cordoba Ibn Bassam calls a meeting place for the free spirits of the city, and in her name he wrote his mocking epistle to Ibn Abdus, his rival for her love. Al-Safadi says he was called “the Buhturi of the West” for the polish of his verse and the ease of its meanings.
